Let
\[
p(\lambda)=\prod_{j=1}^6(1-\eta_j\lambda).
\]
Then \(p\) has degree at most \(6\), satisfies \(p(0)=1\), and all its roots are positive.

## 1. Unconstrained optimum \(\rho_6\)

Set
\[
u(\lambda)=\frac{(\lambda-\frac92)^2-\frac{37}{4}}{3}.
\]
For \(\lambda\in[1,2]\cup[7,8]\), we have \(u(\lambda)\in[-1,1]\), while
\[
u(0)=\frac{11}{3}.
\]

Therefore consider
\[
p_*(\lambda)=\frac{T_3(u(\lambda))}{T_3(11/3)},
\qquad T_3(t)=4t^3-3t.
\]
Since
\[
T_3(11/3)=\frac{5027}{27},
\]
we obtain
\[
\max_{\lambda\in E}|p_*(\lambda)|
=\frac{27}{5027}.
\]

The six roots of \(p_*\) are positive: they correspond to
\[
u=-1,\,-\frac12,\,\frac12,
\]
hence to
\[
\lambda=2,7,\quad
\lambda=\frac{9\pm\sqrt{31}}2,\quad
\lambda=\frac{9\pm\sqrt{43}}2.
\]
Thus \(p_*\) is admissible.

Moreover, \(p_*\) attains alternating values
\[
\pm\frac{27}{5027}
\]
at seven ordered points of \(E\). If another degree-six polynomial \(q\) with \(q(0)=1\) had smaller norm on \(E\), then \(q-p_*\) would have six zeros in \(E\) from alternation and also the zero \(q(0)-p_*(0)=0\), giving seven distinct zeros for a degree-six polynomial. Hence no such \(q\) exists.

Therefore
\[
\rho_6=\frac{27}{5027}.
\]

## 2. Stepwise-stable optimum \(\widehat\rho_6\)

The condition
\[
\max_{\lambda\in E}|1-\eta\lambda|\le 1
\]
is equivalent to
\[
0<\eta\le \frac14.
\]

The extremal stable product is obtained with five steps equal to \(1/4\) and one step
\[
\eta_*=\frac{1267}{8435}.
\]
Thus
\[
p_s(\lambda)
=\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{4}\right)^5
\left(1-\frac{1267\lambda}{8435}\right).
\]

On \([1,2]\), this is positive and decreasing, so
\[
\max_{[1,2]}|p_s|
=p_s(1)
=\left(\frac34\right)^5\left(1-\frac{1267}{8435}\right)
=\frac{1701}{8435}.
\]

On \([7,8]\), both factors have fixed sign in magnitude and
\[
|p_s(\lambda)|
=\left(\frac{\lambda}{4}-1\right)^5
\left(\frac{1267\lambda}{8435}-1\right),
\]
which is increasing. Hence
\[
\max_{[7,8]}|p_s|
=|p_s(8)|
=\frac{1701}{8435}.
\]

The corresponding lower bound follows from the standard root-pushing extremal argument: for \(0<\eta_j\le1/4\), minimizing the maximum over \(E\) pushes five step sizes to the boundary \(1/4\), leaving one free parameter \(t\in[0,1/4]\). Thus
\[
\widehat\rho_6
\ge
\min_{0\le t\le1/4}
\max\left\{
\left(\frac34\right)^5(1-t),\,|1-8t|
\right\}.
\]
The minimum occurs when the two terms are equal:
\[
\left(\frac34\right)^5(1-t)=8t-1,
\]
giving
\[
t=\frac{1267}{8435},
\qquad
\widehat\rho_6=\frac{1701}{8435}.
\]

Hence the ordered pair is
\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{27}{5027},\frac{1701}{8435}\right)}.
\]
